references.text: Describes how Jacob bought Esau's birthright, which is relevant for understanding why Jacob later deceived his father to receive the blessing intended for Esau.
Isaac asks Esau to hunt game and prepare a dish for him so that he can bless Esau before his death, setting the stage for Jacob's deception.
Rebekah devises a plan for Jacob on how he can deceive Isaac and receive the blessing meant for Esau. This is the direct preparation for Jacob's arrival at his father in verse 18.
Esau discovers that Jacob has deceived Isaac and taken the blessing, and complains about Jacob's betrayal—the consequences of the deception that begins in verse 18.
Direct continuation of the same narrative concerning Jacob's deception and Isaac's doubt.
The direct conclusion to Isaac's question about identity in the deception scene.
Contrast between Samuel's verbal response and Jacob's deceitful use of the same response formula.
Direct continuation of the dialogue where Isaac approaches the point of deception.
Theological contrast between Abraham's willing sacrifice scene and Isaac's deception scene involving an exchange of identities.
